The objectives of this notebook will be to conduct a cluster analysis using site-averaged BLM predictor variables to identify a typological classification of samples. This classification will be balled Typology2

This will be conducted under the baseline BLM assumptions (HA 10% Closed System) within the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet Clean version 2.

First, set the working directory

```{r}
setwd("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/5. Cluster analysis")
```

# Identifying Stream Typologies

Using Site average values of BLM predictors.

Import dataset

```{r}
library(readxl)

dat <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/4. Exploratory data analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean2.xlsx", 
    sheet = "HA 10% Closed System")

head(dat)
```

Omit pooled samples

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  filter(Flow_state != "Pooled")

# Check
unique(dat$Flow_state)
```

## 1. Select variables by site

We'll use the scaled, log-transformed BLM predictors to conduct a PCA

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(cluster)

# Variables to select
vars_to_select <- c("log_Temp_C", "pH", "log_DOC_uM",
                    "log_DIC_uM", "log_Cl_uM", "log_Ca_uM", 
                    "log_Mg_uM", "log_SO4_uM", "log_Na_uM", 
                    "log_K_uM", "log_Zn_uM", "log_Cu_uM")

# Scale sample-level chemistry variables
scaled_blm_predict <- as.data.frame(
  scale(dat[vars_to_select])
)

# Add Site back in
scaled_blm_predict$Site <- dat$Site

# Average scaled values by Site
site_means_scaled <- scaled_blm_predict %>%
  group_by(Site) %>%
  summarise(
    across(all_of(vars_to_select), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


```

## 2. K-means clustering

### i. Identifying the number of clusters

Run k-means using 2-5 and identify which number of clusters minimizes the overlap

```{r}
# Create numeric clustering dataset
#    (remove Site before k-means)
cluster_dat <- site_means_scaled %>%
  dplyr::select(-Site)

# Optional safety check
sum(is.na(cluster_dat))
sum(!is.finite(as.matrix(cluster_dat)))

# Silhouette check for k = 2:10
set.seed(123)

sil_df <- lapply(2:5, function(k) {
  
  km <- kmeans(
    cluster_dat,
    centers = k,
    nstart = 50
  )
  
  sil <- silhouette(km$cluster, dist(cluster_dat))
  
  data.frame(
    k = k,
    mean_silhouette = mean(sil[, 3])
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

sil_df
```

### ii. Clustering

Run k-means using 2 clusters

```{r}
# Fit final k-means model
set.seed(123)

final_k <- 2

km_final <- kmeans(
  cluster_dat,
  centers = final_k,
  nstart = 50
)

# Make a Site-level cluster lookup table

site_clusters <- site_means_scaled %>%
  dplyr::select(Site) %>%
  mutate(Typology2 = factor(km_final$cluster))

site_clusters
```

```{r}
# Join Site-level clusters back to sample-level dat
dat_clustered <- dat %>%
  left_join(site_clusters, by = "Site")

# Check result
head(dat_clustered)
table(dat_clustered$Typology2, useNA = "ifany")
```

Assign Cluster to samples in dat

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  left_join(site_clusters, by = "Site")

# Check that every sample received a cluster
sum(is.na(dat$Typology2))

# Look at distribution
table(dat$Typology2)

# Confirm clusters are consistent by site
dat %>%
  group_by(Site) %>%
  summarise(n_clusters = n_distinct(Typology2))
```

## 3. Plot of clusters on PCA

Overlay clusters on PCA

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(factoextra)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 0) Build Site-level table with clusters
#-------------------------------------------------
site_pca_df <- site_means_scaled %>%
  mutate(Typology2 = factor(km_final$cluster))

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1) Force cluster order + set cluster colors
#-------------------------------------------------
typology2_colors <- c(
  "1" = "#56B4E9",
  "2" = "#D55E00"
)

site_pca_df$Typology2 <- factor(site_pca_df$Typology2, levels = c("1", "2", "4", "3"))

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2) Create numeric matrix for PCA
#    (remove Site and Typology2 columns)
#-------------------------------------------------
pca_input <- site_pca_df %>%
  dplyr::select(-Site, -Typology2)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 3) Run PCA on Site-level chemistry
#-------------------------------------------------
pca_result <- prcomp(pca_input, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

pca_summary <- summary(pca_result)

# Optional: view variance explained
pca_summary

#-------------------------------------------------
# 4) Make PCA biplot colored by Site-level cluster
#-------------------------------------------------
pca_typology2 <- fviz_pca_biplot(
  pca_result,
  geom.ind     = "point",
  col.var      = "black",
  habillage    = site_pca_df$Typology2,
  addEllipses  = TRUE,
  legend.title = "Typology2",
  palette      = typology2_colors
) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA Biplot of Sites by Typology2"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

# View plot
pca_typology2

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5) Save plot
#-------------------------------------------------
out_dir <- "Typology2 Plots"

if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "PCA_Biplot_Sites_by_Typology2.png"),
  plot     = pca_typology2,
  width    = 8,
  height   = 6,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

## 4. Characterizing clusters

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 0) Define inherent site characteristics
#-------------------------------------------------
site_char <- c("Type", "Regime", "Development")

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1) Make a SITE-LEVEL dataframe
#    Keep one row per Site with its cluster
#-------------------------------------------------
site_level_chars <- dat_clustered %>%
  dplyr::select(Site, all_of(site_char), Typology2) %>%
  distinct()

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2) Count frequencies and compute relative frequency
#    within each Variable x Cluster combination
#-------------------------------------------------
cluster_summary_table_pct <- site_level_chars %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(site_char),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  count(Variable, Typology2, Value, name = "Freq") %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology2) %>%
  mutate(RelFreq = Freq / sum(Freq) * 100) %>%
  ungroup()

cluster_summary_table_pct

# Save
library(openxlsx)

# 1. Create a brand-new workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

# 2. Add a sheet
addWorksheet(wb, sheetName = "Typology2")

# 3. Write in the sheet with the dataset
writeData(wb, sheet = "Typology2", cluster_summary_table_pct)

# 4. Save
saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  file = "Relative_freq_by_typology2.xlsx",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

Plot

```{r}
#-------------------------------------------------
# 3) Combine variable + value for fill labels
#-------------------------------------------------
cluster_summary_table_pct <- cluster_summary_table_pct %>%
  mutate(Value_labeled = paste0(Variable, ": ", Value))

#-------------------------------------------------
# 4) Set plotting order
#-------------------------------------------------
cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled <- factor(
  cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled,
  levels = c(
    "Type: Tributaries",
    "Type: Main Stem",
    
    "Development: Low",
    "Development: Medium",
    "Development: High",
    
    "Regime: NonPerennial",
    "Regime: Perennial"
  )
)

cluster_summary_table_pct$Variable <- factor(
  cluster_summary_table_pct$Variable,
  levels = c("Type", "Development", "Regime")
)

cluster_summary_table_pct$Typology2 <- factor(
  cluster_summary_table_pct$Typology2,
  levels = c("1", "2")
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5) Define colors
#-------------------------------------------------
color_map <- c(
  "Type: Tributaries" = "#dadaeb",
  "Type: Main Stem" = "#756bb1",
  
  "Development: Low" = "#fdd49e",
  "Development: Medium" = "orange2",
  "Development: High" = "red3",
  
  "Regime: NonPerennial" = "lightblue",
  "Regime: Perennial" = "#1f78a4"
)

# Legend labels without the variable prefix
legend_labels <- gsub("^.*: ", "", levels(cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled))

#-------------------------------------------------
# 6) Plot relative frequencies by cluster
#-------------------------------------------------
rel_freq <- ggplot(
  cluster_summary_table_pct,
  aes(y = Variable, x = RelFreq, fill = Value_labeled)
) +
  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity",
    position = "fill",
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Typology2, ncol = 1, strip.position = "left") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = color_map,
    labels = legend_labels
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Relative Frequency (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.direction = "vertical"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1))

rel_freq

# Save 
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Relative_freq_plots_by_cluster.png"),
  plot     = rel_freq,
  width    = 8,
  height   = 6,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

-   Cluster 1: Non-perennial tributary sites with medium-low developed land cover

-   Cluster 2: Perennial tributaries and main stem sites with more developed land cover

Identify which Sites fall into each Typology2

```{r}
library(dplyr)

sites_by_typology2 <- dat %>%
  distinct(Site, Typology2) %>%
  group_by(Typology2) %>%
  summarise(
    Sites = paste(sort(Site), collapse = ", "),
    n_sites = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sites_by_typology2

# Save
library(openxlsx)

# 1. Create a brand-new workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

# 2. Add a sheet
addWorksheet(wb, sheetName = "Typology2")

# 3. Write in the sheet with the dataset
writeData(wb, sheet = "Typology2", sites_by_typology2)

# 4. Save
saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  file = "sites_by_typology2.xlsx",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

Rename Typology2

```{r}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Typology2 = dplyr::recode(
      Typology2,
      `1` = "Non-Perennial",
      `2` = "Perennial Developed"
    )
  )

unique(dat$Typology2)
```

Save

```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Read in Excel sheet
# --------------------------------------------------
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- "C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/5. Cluster analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean3.xlsx"

sheet_name <- "HA 10% Closed System"

ha10_dat <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = sheet_name)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create Typology2 lookup table from dat
# --------------------------------------------------
typology_lookup <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Typology2) %>%
  distinct()

# Optional check for duplicated Sample_ID values in lookup
typology_lookup %>%
  count(Sample_ID) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Join Typology2 onto Excel data by Sample_ID
# --------------------------------------------------
ha10_dat_updated <- ha10_dat %>%
  left_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Save as a new Excel workbook in working directory
# --------------------------------------------------
output_path <- file.path(getwd(), "Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean3.xlsx")

write.xlsx(
  ha10_dat_updated,
  file = output_path,
  sheetName = sheet_name,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

cat("File saved to:\n", output_path, "\n")
```

## 6. Sites within Typology2

```{r}
library(dplyr)

np_tribs <- dat %>%
  filter(Typology2 == "Non-Perennial") %>%   
  dplyr::select(Site, Typology2) %>%          
  distinct()  

pd_tribs <- dat %>%
  filter(Typology2 == "Perennial Developed") %>%   
  dplyr::select(Site, Typology2) %>%          
  distinct()  

np_tribs
pd_tribs

# Save
out_dir <- "Typology2 Plots"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

library(openxlsx)

# Create workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

# Add worksheets and write data
addWorksheet(wb, "NP Tribs")
writeData(wb, "NP Tribs", np_tribs)

addWorksheet(wb, "PD Tribs")
writeData(wb, "PD Tribs", pd_tribs)


# Save workbook
saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "Sites_by_typology.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```
